criteria: Both sides are the ELBO. Left is log Pθ(x) minus KL(Qφ(z|x) || Pθ(z|x)).
Right is E_{z~Qφ(z|x)}[log Pθ(x|z)] minus KL(Qφ(z|x) || Pθ(z)). Identify the expected log likelihood as the decoder/reconstruction term.
The posterior KL is the nonnegative gap. It is zero exactly when approximate and true posteriors coincide almost everywhere; this is the tight-bound condition.
The other KL compares to the prior, not the posterior. An observation can update the latent distribution away from the prior even under exact inference. This last conclusion is a derivation.
H1.disqualifier: Wrong direction or conditioning of either KL, claiming both vanish, or treating the slide’s approximate-zero callout as an unconditional identity.

criteria: Both images show a handwritten 7.
Input and reconstruction are 784-dimensional; the channel carries a two-dimensional code z.
The encoder f sends the code and the receiver’s decoder g reconstructs from it.
A1.disqualifier: Transmits the full image or calls the channel 784-dimensional.

criteria: Denoising corrupts x by adding noise to obtain x-tilde; the encoder consumes that corrupted input.
Colorization removes color; the encoder consumes the grayscale observation.
In both graphs the latent h drives decoding and the original x supplies the target: clean image for denoising, color image for colorization.
A2.disqualifier: Uses the corrupted observation as reconstruction target or swaps the slide assignments.

criteria: On the left the encoder yields μ and σ and a sampling node supplies the decoder input.
On the right ε is sampled from N(0,I), separately from the encoder. Multiply it by σ then add μ to form z.
The deterministic path from μ and σ lets the reconstruction gradient reach the encoder; the independent noise draw does not acquire trainable parameters.
V1.disqualifier: Multiplication/addition reversed, or says the encoder samples ε.

criteria: Base loss is L_R + L_KL.
Weighted loss is L_R + β L_KL, so β weights the divergence term only.
The stronger-regularization regime on the slide is β > 1.
V2.disqualifier: Weights reconstruction or claims β must always equal a fixed value.

criteria: Discriminator step: fake target 0 (real 1); update D and stop gradients to G.
Generator step: fake target 1 to make D treat it as real.
D parameters are frozen during the generator update, but gradients pass through D to update G.
G1.disqualifier: Says frozen D blocks the generator gradient or swaps fake targets.

criteria: The generator receives z and one-hot y-prime to produce the synthetic x-prime.
D receives fake paired with its condition y-prime or real x paired with the one-hot y.
Class labels specify which class; the separate binary labels encode fake 0 vs real 1.
G2.disqualifier: Treats the class labels as the binary real/fake targets.

criteria: The displayed panel has four rows and four columns, 16 tiles.
Tiles show light handwritten-looking marks on dark squares; condition range 0–9 does not imply ten displayed tiles.
No numerical classification accuracy can be read from these sample images.
G3.disqualifier: Invents per-class accuracy or uses the number of classes as the sample count.

criteria: The example is the digit 7.
Generation/prediction goes from Gaussian X to data Y, Y=U(X), rightward.
Normalization/learning goes from data Y to Gaussian X, X=U⁻¹(Y), leftward.
F1.disqualifier: Swaps U with its inverse or asserts a different digit.

criteria: Inverse block Jacobian is triangular with upper-right zero and upper-left identity.
Lower-right diagonal has entries exp(−s_i(x_1:d)); inverting the forward scale produces the minus sign.
log|det J|=−Σ_i s_i; under the supplied two scales the result is −ln 6 (determinant 1/6).
F2.disqualifier: Uses the positive forward sign or confuses the log determinant with 1/6.

criteria: The table reports average test negative log-likelihood in bits per dimension, lower is better.
Flow++ × MNIST is blank; explicitly say it is unreported.
Give a correct adjacent value labeled with its row/column, e.g. Flow++ on CIFAR-10 is 3.08 or Residual Flow on MNIST is 0.97.
F3.disqualifier: Reports a numerical score for the blank cell, including zero.

criteria: In the AE diagram the 784-dimensional image is encoded to a 2-D z then reconstructed to 784 dimensions.
The flow diagram explicitly labels a reversible bijection; Gaussian-to-digit uses U and the reverse uses U⁻¹.
Approximate reconstruction through a bottleneck does not establish exact inversion on the full input space; an output visually resembling its input is insufficient.
X1.disqualifier: Transfers the flow’s exact-inverse guarantee to the autoencoder.

criteria: Page 26 shows colored scatter plots of latent coordinates.
Page 27 shows grids of decoded digit images. Both slides put the autoencoder on the left and the VAE on the right.
Neither comparison supplies a numerical reconstruction error.
V3.disqualifier: Reverses the two visual types/models or invents a reconstruction metric.
